subject: Lightweight SIEM egress proxy & telemetry gating for private deployments
messages:

Subject: Telemetry egress for private deployment - quick design call?

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry egress for private deployment - quick design call?

Hi Alex — thanks, this is straightforward to scope. I put together a compact proposal and attached a one-page reference (egress-proxy-arch.v1.pdf) plus a CSV of suggested SIEM field mappings. Key points up-front:

1) Single outbound endpoint: a customer-configurable "egress proxy" (mutual-TLS) that we host inside the customer's VPC (sidecar/hosted container).
   - Only outbound allowed: kube/node -> Egress Proxy (TLS 443) -> Customer SIEM / Log Forwarder
   - Egress Proxy does batching, rate-limiting, and per-batch signing (HMAC) so the SIEM can verify integrity.

2) Auth & trust model:
   - mTLS between agents -> proxy.
   - Proxy signs envelopes with a customer-provided key (HSM/KMS optional).
   - Optional JWT attestation for token-based revocation.

3) PII/redaction layer:
   - We recommend a configurable pre-forward sanitization step (regex + field allowlist) run in the proxy.
   - Default policy: remove full-text user prompts and keep metadata + anonymized hash.

4) Tracing hooks:
   - OpenTelemetry spans exported to the proxy over OTLP/HTTP.
   - Proxy preserves trace context (W3C traceparent) and forwards minimal sampled spans to SIEM.

5) Operational checklist for Net/Sec (what you asked for):
   - Allow outbound to proxy IP(s)/DNS on TCP 443 only.
   - Provide CIDR(s) for host-level peers if using managed proxy pool.
   - Provide list of required cert thumbprints for initial bootstrap.
   - Cert rotation cadence: 90 days recommended; hot-reload supported.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal quick sync (30m) to confirm defaults we should ship in the starter config (kimberly + karthik + marissa)
- Handshake call with MedBridge SecOps to walk the one-pager and checklist (I can host today at 4pm PT or tomorrow morning)

Attachments: egress-proxy-arch.v1.pdf, siem-field-mapping.csv

--
Stephanie Nguyen

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example

Subject: Re: Telemetry egress for private deployment - quick design call?

Looping in a couple of quick technical notes — replying all so Alex sees the consolidated plan after our internal alignment.

Stephanie — I like the egress-proxy approach. A few implementation considerations from the observability side:

- Trace sampling: keep default sampling at 1% for long-ish traces, with a sampler rule to retain 100% of error spans for the first 30s after an incident flag. We can surface sampled traces into the SIEM as compact JSON (selected span ids + tags).

- Telemetry transport: prefer OTLP/HTTP with gzip; OTLP over GRPC was rejected by one partner because of blocked ports. OTLP/HTTP reduces connection churn and is simpler to forward from the proxy.

- Agent footprint: provide both a node-level forwarder (Fluentd/Vector lightweight config) and an optional sidecar. For regulated customers we recommend node-level forwarder to keep logs local until redaction completes.

- Mapping & enrichment: the attached CSV is a good start. Add these fields: customer_account_id, deployment_region, redaction_level, forwarded_by (proxy-id).

- Failure modes: proxy should have a bounded disk spool (configurable) and backpressure handling (reject after spool full + alert). Default spool = 10GB.

Action items for our sync:
- Marissa: confirm default spool size & retention preset for Private Quickstart.
- Karthik: confirm auth flow for KMS-backed signing and a fallback HMAC mode.
- Stephanie: get final go/no-go on attaching the sanitization plugin by default.

Kimberly Park
Senior Infra Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example
To: Alex Benitez <alex.benitez@medbridge.com>
Cc: secops@medbridge.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry egress for private deployment - quick design call?

Alex — thanks for the prompt. Quick summary / decision items from our side that we can present to SecOps: 

- Approach: deploy a lightweight egress proxy inside your VPC (container or DaemonSet) that accepts OTLP/HTTP and syslog-like envelopes, performs sanitization, batching, and signs batches before forwarding to your SIEM.

- Network allowlist: we only need outbound to the egress proxy host(s) on TCP 443. If you prefer a managed proxy pool, we'll provide a CIDR and FQDN for your perimeter rules.

- Auth: mTLS for agent->proxy; proxy->siem will use signed envelopes (HMAC) plus optional mTLS depending on your SIEM. We can support KMS/HSM key material if you require BYOK.

- Data protection: default sanitization removes free-text prompts and retains hashed identifiers. We will provide a policy you can enforce/modify in the proxy config before any data leaves your VPC.

- Ops & runbook: I've attached the one-pager and mapping CSV. Proposed handshake: 30 mins tomorrow 10am PT to walk SecOps through: ports/CIDRs, cert thumbprints, and the cert rotation checklist.

Please confirm the time or propose an alternative. If you prefer, we can run the first verification on a staging VPC with minimal sample traffic.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
